$comment: Historical goals with their reasons for western Europe, the Empire, Italy and the Nordic realms (plan-1378 §2), from start-date/research/europe-west.md. Weighed by the AI (EVT-100 to EVT-106); never forced.

goals.goal: Hold Calais, Gascony, Brest and Cherbourg and win back Aquitaine
goals.reason: The French reconquest of 1369 to 1375 took most of the 1360 lands; the crown's claim and the lords' honour rest on them
goals.ends_when: All French lands lost, or a lasting peace with territory
goals.deviation: A long truce and a French marriage, as Richard did in 1396

goals.goal: Press the claim to the French crown
goals.reason: The dynasty's main source of prestige; after 1399 a source of legitimacy for Lancaster
goals.deviation: Use the claim only as a bargaining chip for Aquitaine

goals.goal: Put John of Gaunt on the throne of Castile
goals.reason: Gaunt's claim through his wife Constance; it would break France's naval ally
goals.ends_when: Gaunt dies, or a marriage settles it (Bayonne 1388)
goals.deviation: Settle for a marriage of Gaunt's daughter into the Trastámara house and a pension

goals.goal: Keep the Portuguese alliance
goals.reason: Portuguese ports and fleet against Castile
goals.deviation: Back a Portuguese candidate in a succession crisis (Avis 1385)

goals.goal: Contain Scotland and keep the border lordships
goals.reason: The Scots are France's ally and raid the March
goals.ends_when: Scotland is subject, or a stable peace
goals.deviation: A truce and a marriage, as in 1424

goals.goal: Pay for the war without a revolt
goals.reason: The poll taxes of 1377 to 1381 break the countryside's patience
goals.deviation: Cut back the war to avoid taxation

goals.goal: Restore royal lordship in Ireland
goals.reason: Black rent and the Gaelic recovery shrink the colony
goals.ends_when: The Pale is secure, or England is too busy
goals.deviation: Leave Ireland to the strongest earl

goals.goal: Recover Berwick, Roxburgh, Annandale and the border castles
goals.reason: Lost in the wars of independence; national honour and the border lords' lands
goals.ends_when: Places taken, or a lasting peace
goals.deviation: Live with truces and raid only

goals.goal: Keep the French alliance
goals.reason: It pays and protects Scotland against England
goals.ends_when: France makes a separate peace or collapses

goals.goal: Settle Stewart power through the king's sons
goals.reason: Robert II rules by giving the great earldoms to his family
goals.ends_when: A strong king curbs them (James I from 1424)
goals.deviation: A magnate (Douglas) takes the lead instead

goals.goal: Gain the earldom of Ross
goals.reason: A claim through the Leslie heiress from 1402; Ross gives a mainland power base
goals.ends_when: Ross held, or the claim lost
goals.deviation: Expand into Lochaber and the Ulster Glens instead

goals.goal: Keep autonomy from the Stewart crown
goals.reason: A semi-royal Gaelic lordship with its own council

goals.goal: Win land in Ulster
goals.reason: Galloglass trade and marriage links

goals.goal: Defend the Pale and stop the black rent
goals.reason: Gaelic lords tax the colony
goals.ends_when: A strong governor with English money

goals.goal: Recover the earldom of Ulster for Mortimer
goals.reason: The Mortimer heir holds the Ulster and Connacht claims
goals.ends_when: The Mortimer line fails or Ulster is lost

goals.goal: Overlordship of Ulster
goals.reason: O'Neill claims the high kingship of the north and the old earldom's land
goals.ends_when: O'Neill weakened, or a strong English deputy
goals.deviation: Submit to the king for recognition (as in 1395)

goals.goal: Win the kingship of Leinster and the colony's fees
goals.reason: Art Mór claims the Norfolk lands in Leinster through his wife, and black rent
goals.ends_when: Crushed, or the fee is paid
goals.deviation: Submit for a fee and a title, as in 1395

goals.goal: Hold the governorship or act as a regional king
goals.reason: Office brings revenue and patronage; a weak crown leaves a vacuum
goals.deviation: Gaelicise and rule as a Gaelic lord

goals.goal: Hold the governorship or act as a regional king
goals.reason: Office brings revenue and patronage; a weak crown leaves a vacuum

goals.goal: Hold the governorship or act as a regional king
goals.reason: Office brings revenue and patronage; a weak crown leaves a vacuum

goals.goal: Secure the Trastámara crown against Lancaster
goals.reason: A usurping dynasty, and John of Gaunt claims the throne
goals.deviation: Defeat Gaunt in the field and keep France's backing

goals.goal: Keep the French alliance and the war at sea against England
goals.reason: France made the dynasty; galleys win prestige and plunder
goals.deviation: Neutrality if France fails to pay

goals.goal: Win Portugal by marriage or war
goals.reason: Ferdinand's only heir is Beatriz; union would remove a rival allied to England
goals.deviation: Settle for border gains and peace (as in 1411)

goals.goal: Bend Navarre
goals.reason: Navarre is England's door into Iberia

goals.goal: Buy the great nobles with grants
goals.reason: Henry's victory rests on them
goals.ends_when: The crown is strong enough to reclaim grants
goals.deviation: Rule through favourites (later Álvaro de Luna)

goals.goal: Push the Granada frontier
goals.reason: Crusading tradition and tribute (parias)
goals.deviation: Keep the truce and the tribute

goals.goal: Conquer Sardinia from Arborea
goals.reason: The papal grant of 1297; trade, grain and Catalan honour
goals.deviation: Make peace with Arborea and hold the towns only

goals.goal: Gain Sicily for the House of Barcelona
goals.reason: Family right after Frederick III's death; Catalan trade
goals.deviation: Rule Sicily through a cadet (Martin the Younger)

goals.goal: Hold the Catalan duchies in Greece
goals.reason: Catalan honour and trade

goals.goal: Keep Majorca against Anjou's claim
goals.reason: The Majorcan claim passed to Louis of Anjou

goals.goal: Stay out of the Schism and the Anglo-French war
goals.reason: Peter weighs both sides for gain
goals.deviation: Declare early for Avignon for French favour

goals.goal: Keep the peace with Castile
goals.reason: Almazán ended a ruinous war

goals.goal: Claim the Castilian crown
goals.reason: Ferdinand's descent from Sancho IV and the Trastámara illegitimacy

goals.goal: Keep the English alliance
goals.reason: A counterweight to Castile

goals.goal: Defend independence in the succession crisis
goals.reason: Ferdinand's heir is a girl promised to Castile

goals.goal: Turn to Morocco and the Atlantic
goals.reason: The nobility and the orders need land; trade

goals.goal: Recover the Norman lands and Montpellier
goals.reason: Charles II's inheritance was seized in 1378
goals.deviation: Trade them for a French duchy

goals.goal: Survive between France, Castile and England
goals.reason: A small kingdom open on all sides
goals.deviation: Lean fully on Castile after Briones

goals.goal: Control the Strait and the Marinid court
goals.reason: Gibraltar and Ceuta guard Granada; a friendly Fez protects it
goals.ends_when: Marinid power independent, or the Strait lost

goals.goal: Keep the peace with Castile without tribute
goals.reason: Castile is far stronger

goals.goal: Drive the English out of Gascony, Calais, Brest and Cherbourg
goals.reason: The reconquest of 1369 to 1375 left a few footholds that keep the English claim alive
goals.ends_when: France holds Bordeaux, Bayonne and Calais, or a lasting peace
goals.deviation: Accept a long truce and turn to Flanders and Italy (Leulinghem 1389)

goals.goal: Annex or tame Brittany
goals.reason: John IV sided with England; the crown wants Brittany's coast closed to English fleets
goals.ends_when: Brittany is royal, or a duke does homage and cuts off England
goals.deviation: Back a Penthièvre duke as a client instead

goals.goal: Destroy Charles the Bad's power in France
goals.reason: Navarrese plots and Norman ports opened France to England
goals.ends_when: Navarre holds no fiefs in France, or takes compensation
goals.deviation: A settlement with Charles III (lands exchanged for Nemours, 1404)

goals.goal: Bring the Church to the French pope
goals.reason: A French pope at Avignon is a political asset and a source of revenue
goals.deviation: Neutrality and the way of cession (subtraction, 1398)

goals.goal: Clear the routiers from the centre
goals.reason: Free Companies ruin the tax base of Auvergne and the Limousin
goals.ends_when: The companies are bought out or crushed
goals.deviation: Lead them abroad (Castile, Italy) instead of buying them out

goals.goal: Secure the Flemish inheritance
goals.reason: His wife is heiress of Flanders, Artois, Nevers, Rethel and the Franche-Comté
goals.deviation: Barter parts of it for royal favour or money

goals.goal: Dominate the royal council
goals.reason: A prince of the blood gains pensions, offices and royal armies (Roosebeke 1382)
goals.ends_when: A rival party controls the king (Orléans from 1392, Armagnac from 1410)
goals.deviation: Turn to the Low Countries and the Empire alone

goals.goal: Keep Flanders' wool trade with England
goals.reason: Flemish towns need English wool, and Ghent revolts (1379 to 1385)
goals.deviation: A trade truce with England separate from France

goals.goal: Restore the duke and ducal autonomy
goals.reason: John IV is exiled and the king seeks to annex the duchy
goals.ends_when: The duke rules from Vannes and Nantes with his privileges (Guérande 1381)
goals.deviation: Accept a Penthièvre duke if John IV dies

goals.goal: Recover Brest from England
goals.reason: The lease was the price of English help, and Bretons resent the garrison
goals.deviation: Keep the English alliance as a check on France

goals.goal: Keep the Penthièvre down
goals.reason: The Blois claim survives Auray and Guérande
goals.ends_when: The Penthièvre are crushed or reconciled
goals.deviation: Marry into them for peace (the 1380s attempts)

goals.goal: Stay tied to whichever Angevin wins Naples
goals.reason: The barons and towns split on Joanna's succession (Union of Aix 1382 to 1387)
goals.ends_when: One heir is recognised by the estates (1387)
goals.deviation: Towns such as Nice seek another protector (Savoy, 1388)

goals.goal: Hold the Durance and the Rhône against neighbours
goals.reason: Routiers, Savoy and the Dauphiné press on its borders

goals.goal: Win the crown of Naples
goals.reason: Joanna adopts him (1380) and Clement VII backs him; a kingdom outranks an apanage
goals.ends_when: He holds Naples, or the Angevin claim is extinct
goals.deviation: Settle for Provence and influence in France

goals.goal: Hold the regency and the purse
goals.reason: The eldest uncle on the king's death needs money for Italy

goals.goal: Control Languedoc and its taxes
goals.reason: The richest royal lieutenancy funds his court

goals.goal: Keep a share of power between Burgundy and Orléans
goals.reason: As the elder uncle he wants a peace among princes that keeps his place
goals.deviation: Join the Orléans and Armagnac side (League of Gien, 1410)

goals.goal: Serve and guard the boy king
goals.reason: He is the king's uncle on the mother's side and a crusading knight

goals.goal: Clear the routiers from the Bourbonnais and Auvergne
goals.reason: His lands border the routier country

goals.goal: Keep Béarn sovereign and neutral
goals.reason: Fébus holds Béarn of God alone and plays England against France
goals.ends_when: Béarn is subdued, or his line ends (1391)
goals.deviation: Seek the Languedoc lieutenancy (1380) against Berry

goals.goal: Keep Bigorre and the Pyrenean passes
goals.reason: They tie Foix to Béarn
goals.deviation: Trade them for peace with Armagnac

goals.goal: Build a great southern principality (Comminges, Bigorre)
goals.reason: Armagnac rivals Foix and leads the southern lords
goals.ends_when: It holds them, or is crushed (1443 to 1444)
goals.deviation: Buy the routiers and lead them to Italy (John III, 1391)

goals.goal: Serve the crown against England
goals.reason: French since 1368, with lands bordering Gascony
goals.ends_when: The English are gone from the south
goals.deviation: Change sides when the crown weakens (the 1440s English approach)

goals.goal: Hold the coastal footholds
goals.reason: Calais and Bordeaux carry the wool and wine trades; Brest and Cherbourg guard against invasion
goals.ends_when: They are lost or traded in a peace
goals.deviation: Trade Brest and Cherbourg for a truce (done 1394 to 1397)

goals.goal: Live by ransoms from their castles
goals.reason: Unpaid soldiers with fortresses and an English excuse
goals.ends_when: They are bought out or beaten
goals.deviation: Sell their castles and take service in Italy or Castile

goals.goal: Win power at court against Burgundy
goals.reason: The king's brother needs the treasury and the regency during the madness
goals.ends_when: Louis is murdered (1407), or Burgundy is broken
goals.deviation: Make peace with Burgundy through a marriage

goals.goal: Press the Visconti claim to Asti and Milan
goals.reason: Valentina Visconti's dowry (Asti) and her rights to Milan
goals.ends_when: The Visconti line holds, or Orléans holds Milan

goals.goal: Bring Ghent to heel
goals.reason: Ghent's privileges and its veto on the Bruges canal block the count's revenue and control
goals.ends_when: Ghent is subdued, or the count dies
goals.deviation: Buy peace with charters (the count needs money)

goals.goal: Keep the wool trade with England open while staying a French vassal
goals.reason: Flemish cloth needs English wool; the count owes homage to France
goals.ends_when: The Burgundian succession fixes the line
goals.deviation: Lean to England if France presses

goals.goal: Secure Margaret's inheritance for Burgundy
goals.reason: She is the only heir; Philip the Bold protects the count against the towns
goals.deviation: Seek another match only if Philip dies

goals.goal: Defend its staple and privileges against the count and Bruges
goals.reason: The Bruges canal and new taxes threaten Ghent's grain and cloth
goals.ends_when: Peace on good terms, or crushed

goals.goal: Ally with England
goals.reason: England is Urbanist and the wool supplier; the Artevelde precedent

goals.goal: Avenge Baesweiler and hold Grave and the Meuse
goals.reason: The 1371 defeat; border towns lost or pawned to Guelders and Jülich

goals.goal: Recover Antwerp and Mechelen
goals.reason: Lost to Flanders in 1357
goals.deviation: Accept a Burgundian Antwerp if a Burgundian heir is named

goals.goal: Settle the succession
goals.reason: Joanna is childless, and the estates are bound by the Joyous Entry

goals.goal: Keep the duchy solvent and the lords at peace
goals.reason: Wenceslaus I is in debt from the Baesweiler ransom and his landfrieden
goals.deviation: Pawn lands (as the next rulers did)

goals.goal: Hold the Hook and Cod parties in balance
goals.reason: The parties tore the county in the 1350s; Albert rules as regent

goals.goal: Win Frisia
goals.reason: An old comital claim; Frisian feuds give openings
goals.ends_when: Frisia taken, or the claim given up
goals.deviation: Settle for tribute or alliances with chieftains (tom Brok)

goals.goal: Marry the house into the Burgundian circle
goals.reason: Security against France and Brabant (the 1385 double wedding at Cambrai)
goals.deviation: Marry into England or the Empire

goals.goal: Subdue Arkel and the river lords
goals.reason: They control the Merwede and the Linge

goals.goal: Win the succession war
goals.reason: Mathilda's party holds towns; the investiture alone is not enough

goals.goal: Take Grave and the Meuse from Brabant
goals.reason: Strategic river towns; Brabant hostile since Baesweiler

goals.goal: Ally with England against France and Burgundy
goals.reason: Brabant is French-backed; English money
goals.ends_when: The French or Burgundian threat is gone
goals.deviation: Make peace with France after the 1388 invasion

goals.goal: Put his son on the Guelders throne
goals.reason: A family claim through Mary of Guelders

goals.goal: Keep Aachen and the Lower Rhine landfrieden in his favour
goals.reason: The advocacy of Aachen; toll and robber-knight disputes

goals.goal: Win ducal rank and grow on the right bank
goals.reason: Berg is rising against Cologne and Mark

goals.goal: Inherit Jülich
goals.reason: The same house; the Jülich-Guelders line may die out
goals.ends_when: Inheritance (1423), or a new Jülich heir

goals.goal: Unite Cleves and the Mark
goals.reason: The brothers' lands; Engelbert III has no male heir

goals.goal: Keep Jülich out of Guelders
goals.reason: A Jülich-Guelders block would surround Cleves
goals.deviation: Make peace and seek Burgundian ties

goals.goal: Hold its own against Cologne
goals.reason: Rhine tolls and the Westphalian borders

goals.goal: Win Dortmund's lordship or its money
goals.reason: A rich imperial city in the middle of the Mark

goals.goal: Govern with the estates under the Peace of the XXII
goals.reason: The towns enforce the 1316 and 1373 settlements
goals.ends_when: A bishop breaks them (John of Bavaria, 1390s to 1408)
goals.deviation: The bishop seeks outside help to rule alone

goals.goal: Keep the see Urbanist
goals.reason: Urban VI made Arnold bishop; Clement names a rival
goals.deviation: Accept Clement if Brabant and France press

goals.goal: Hold the Oversticht towns and Drenthe together
goals.reason: They are cut off by the Veluwe, and the IJssel towns act alone
goals.deviation: Let the towns go their own way

goals.goal: Keep Holland and Guelders out
goals.reason: Both press on the Sticht
goals.deviation: Ally with one against the other

goals.goal: Pay off debts and hold the Rhine tolls
goals.reason: Debts from earlier archbishops; tolls are the main revenue

goals.goal: Master the city of Cologne
goals.reason: The city fought the archbishop until 1377

goals.goal: Hold Westphalia against Mark and Dortmund
goals.reason: Westphalia was bought in 1368, and Mark encroaches
goals.deviation: Ally with Mark against Dortmund (as in 1388)

goals.goal: Keep its freedom from the archbishop
goals.reason: Worringen (1288) and the war of 1375 to 1377

goals.goal: Settle its own government
goals.reason: Patrician feuds; the guilds want a share

goals.goal: Win the see against Louis of Meissen
goals.reason: The chapter's choice against Charles IV's

goals.goal: Use the Schism to get confirmation
goals.reason: Clement VII offers what Urban and Charles refused

goals.goal: Contain Hesse and keep the Hessian enclaves
goals.reason: Fritzlar and Amöneburg sit inside Hesse

goals.goal: Build up the territory and its finances
goals.reason: Kuno inherited debts; Koblenz and the Moselle lands

goals.goal: Back the Roman pope and Wenceslaus
goals.reason: Kuno is a Luxembourg ally

goals.goal: Lead the Rhine princes against the city leagues
goals.reason: The leagues threaten princely tolls and lordship
goals.deviation: Make a landfriede with the cities

goals.goal: Recover the Upper Palatinate and the family's rank
goals.reason: Charles IV took parts of it as New Bohemia
goals.ends_when: Recovered, or the Luxembourg crown falls

goals.goal: Put a Palatine on the German throne
goals.reason: Wenceslaus is weak and Rupert III is able

goals.goal: Survive the Mainz, Brunswick and Thuringia coalition
goals.reason: Neighbours eye the Hessian fiefs; Kassel besieged in 1385

goals.goal: Absorb Ziegenhain, Waldeck and Katzenelnbogen
goals.reason: Inheritance pacts and pledges

goals.goal: Win over Metz
goals.reason: A rich free city inside the duchy

goals.goal: Serve and lean on France
goals.reason: John I is in French service
goals.deviation: Turn to Burgundy (as Charles II did)

goals.goal: Keep the Frisian freedom
goals.reason: Holland's claim and the chieftains' ambitions
goals.deviation: One party calls in Holland or Groningen

goals.goal: Unite East Frisia under the tom Brok
goals.reason: Ocko I and his heirs build a lordship over the chieftains
goals.deviation: Ally with Holland or the Hanse

goals.goal: Hold the Emsland and the Lippe border
goals.reason: Tecklenburg and Mark press on them

goals.goal: Secure Wenceslaus's succession
goals.reason: Charles IV bought the electors' votes so the crown stays Luxembourg
goals.deviation: A weak succession invites a rival king early

goals.goal: Back Urban VI and end the Schism
goals.reason: The Empire protects the Church, and Urban crowns emperors in Rome
goals.deviation: Neutrality, as the electors chose in 1438

goals.goal: Keep the public peace between princes and city leagues
goals.reason: The Swabian and Rhenish city leagues fight the princes
goals.deviation: Side openly with the princes or the towns

goals.goal: Depose a negligent king
goals.reason: The electors resent Wenceslaus's absence and his sale of Milan's ducal title
goals.deviation: Wenceslaus stays if he governs the Empire

goals.goal: Keep the Mark and its vote in Luxembourg hands
goals.reason: Two of seven votes make the house kingmaker
goals.deviation: Pledge it for cash, as Jobst got it in 1388

goals.goal: Raise money from the Mark
goals.reason: Sigismund needs funds for his Hungarian marriage and crown

goals.goal: Restrain the robber nobility (the Quitzows)
goals.reason: Absent lords leave the Mark lawless
goals.deviation: Leave it to the towns' leagues

goals.goal: Win Lüneburg for the Ascanians
goals.reason: Charles IV's grant of 1370 and the 1373 settlement
goals.ends_when: Wenceslaus of Saxony dies or Winsen is lost (1388)
goals.deviation: Settle for the alternation and marriages

goals.goal: Hold the electoral vote against Lauenburg
goals.reason: The Golden Bull gave the vote to Wittenberg

goals.goal: Divide the inheritance among the brothers
goals.reason: Three adult brothers, each with heirs

goals.goal: Win the Saxon electorate
goals.reason: A vote and a duke's rank; Wittenberg's line is thin
goals.deviation: Seek Brandenburg or Bohemian land instead

goals.goal: Place Ludwig in a great see
goals.reason: Church provision for a younger son

goals.goal: Hold the Bohemian border
goals.reason: Luxembourg power next door, later the Hussites

goals.goal: Recover Lüneburg from the Ascanians
goals.reason: Welf house law makes them the heirs

goals.goal: Subdue Lüneburg town
goals.reason: The town expelled the dukes and backs the Ascanians
goals.deviation: Leave the town free for its salt money

goals.goal: Throw off Otto the Evil's regency
goals.reason: Frederick is of age and Otto treats the lands as his own

goals.goal: Bring Brunswick city to heel
goals.reason: The city holds ducal pledges and resists

goals.goal: Seek a crown through Frederick's candidacy
goals.reason: Frederick is a leading prince of the reform party

goals.goal: Rule the Brunswick lands
goals.reason: The 1370 succession pact with Magnus II

goals.goal: Feud with Hesse and the towns
goals.reason: Otto's way of rule, and the Sterner knights' cause

goals.goal: Put Albert IV on the Danish throne
goals.reason: Ingeborg's line is senior to Margaret's
goals.ends_when: Albert IV dies (1388) or Margaret rules unopposed

goals.goal: Keep Albert king in Sweden
goals.reason: Family prestige, and Swedish castles and revenues
goals.ends_when: Albert loses at Åsle (1389) and is freed (1395)

goals.goal: Wage privateer war on Denmark
goals.reason: To relieve Stockholm through the Victual Brothers

goals.goal: Win Schleswig as a hereditary fief
goals.reason: They hold most of it by pledge and want the title

goals.goal: Subdue Dithmarschen
goals.reason: The free peasants block the west coast

goals.goal: Reunite the Schauenburg lines
goals.reason: The Kiel and Plön line has no heir

goals.goal: Keep the Stralsund settlement
goals.reason: It gave the towns the Sound trade and the Scanian castles
goals.ends_when: Castles returned (1385) or Denmark breaks the terms

goals.goal: Keep the Baltic safe from pirates
goals.reason: Trade loses ships and goods

goals.goal: Defend the Kontore
goals.reason: Bruges, London, Bergen and Novgorod carry its trade

goals.goal: Keep member towns governed by their councils
goals.reason: Guild risings like Brunswick's in 1374 threaten the order

goals.goal: Lead the Hanse
goals.reason: Directing town since Stralsund

goals.goal: Gain land along the road to Hamburg
goals.reason: The overland route and the Mölln pledge

goals.goal: Hold the lower Elbe
goals.reason: Its trade needs the river mouth

goals.goal: Loosen Schauenburg lordship
goals.reason: Self-government

goals.goal: Get back into the Hanse
goals.reason: Exclusion cuts its trade

goals.goal: Settle the council
goals.reason: The Great Schicht split the city

goals.goal: Help the Welf kin in Lüneburg
goals.reason: Archbishop Albert is a Welf
goals.deviation: Stay neutral and pay off debts

goals.goal: Assert lordship over the city and the marshes
goals.reason: Revenue and rights

goals.goal: Serve Luxembourg policy
goals.reason: Archbishop Peter was placed by Charles IV
goals.deviation: Lean to the Wettins, who take the see in 1381

goals.goal: Control the towns of Magdeburg and Halle
goals.reason: Revenue and authority

goals.goal: Keep the Welfs out
goals.reason: Dinklar (1367) and the ducal threat
goals.ends_when: The Welfs unite against the see

goals.goal: Keep the Luxembourg friendship
goals.reason: Sigismund is a Griffin grandson, which shields them from Brandenburg

goals.goal: Take the Uckermark
goals.reason: Brandenburg is weak under absent lords

goals.goal: Win a crown for the Stolp line
goals.reason: Wartislaw VII's son Eric is Margaret's grandnephew
goals.ends_when: Eric adopted (1389) or the line fails

goals.goal: Claim the Saxon vote
goals.reason: Lauenburg sees itself as the senior Ascanian line
goals.ends_when: The vote passes to the Wettins (1423)

goals.goal: Redeem Mölln and Bergedorf
goals.reason: Pledged to Lübeck

goals.goal: Stay free of Holstein
goals.reason: Kin groups and parishes rule themselves

goals.goal: Win Hungary and Poland for Sigismund
goals.reason: Louis I has only daughters; Sigismund is betrothed to Mary
goals.ends_when: Sigismund crowned in Hungary, or Mary marries elsewhere

goals.goal: Keep both Luxembourg votes and the imperial crown
goals.reason: The Bohemian and Brandenburg votes secure the succession
goals.ends_when: Brandenburg pledged away (1388) or Wenceslaus deposed
goals.deviation: Trade Brandenburg for money, as Sigismund did

goals.goal: End the Schism for Rome and be crowned emperor there
goals.reason: Charles IV's policy and the Urbanist league
goals.deviation: Deal with France on a joint solution (Reims 1398)

goals.goal: Rule through lesser men against the great lords
goals.reason: Royal domain and favourites against the barons
goals.deviation: Rule with the barons and the Rosenbergs
